title: Running through July 23rd (on weeknights only) at The Cell via Most U...
transcript: You are a first grader in Ms. Joy's classroom as she slowly has a breakdown. That's the premise of this interactive, immersive theatre piece that has you doing all sorts of activities like drawing and writing prompts, solving word problems, and other lessons that transport you back to elementary school in a way that's almost frighteningly vivid. But that's not the only frightening thing at play, because creeping into these lessons are increasingly alarming signs that Ms. Joy is dealing with something pretty troubling in her personal life. The play is fittingly called Big Feelings, as it paints a thought provoking portrait of how we process our emotions on a fundamental level and how the way we're encouraged or discouraged as children can shape who we become. The show is right up my alley, and it consistently nails the effects that it's going for. The interactive parts are fun, The way that she interjects her personal baggage into the lessons is hilarious until it takes a dark turn, at which point it becomes genuinely quite chilling. Likewise, watching all of this unfold while we are essentially under her supervision, in her control, gives the play even more unsettling immediacy. I will admit that the show requires a bit of suspension of disbelief. Sometimes it feels like it's pushing the limits of plausibility within this sort of immersive concept. But even at the points where there was a bit of strain between the content and the format, I was enjoying it enough that I wanted to give it the benefit of a more generous read. I was willing to buy into the sometimes heightened, sometimes warped sense of reality that went beyond the literal classroom setting. And when I was confused, it felt like riddles that I was genuinely interested in trying to solve, even if I didn't always succeed. So overall, an exciting theatrical experience that left a lot to chew on.
